lines.speaker: plant_supervisor
lines.text: Twelve-hour shifts, suit on, forty-one degrees in the hot aisle. You get used to the noise about a month before you get used to the heat.

lines.speaker: plant_supervisor
lines.text: What's it doing? Allocation modelling. Housing, work, medicine — who gets what, and when, and how much. Somebody has to decide that and people are genuinely terrible at it. I've seen people do it.

lines.speaker: plant_supervisor
lines.text: And it is better at it than we are. Measurably. I've read the outputs, I've checked them against the old human ones, and it is not close. That is not the part that bothers me.

choices.text: What's the part that bothers you?
Nothing is better at it than we are.

lines.speaker: plant_supervisor
lines.text: The clause went through with a name in it. Whoever managed that — my shift lead has been reading the custody schedule out loud in the canteen all week, doing the voices. First time anything from that senate has been funny.
